core_principles.text: Narrow-width push-ups can be utilized as an advanced variation of traditional shoulder-width push-ups to target the triceps brachii with greater intensity.

specific_findings.text: In a study of a 25-year-old male gymnast, narrow-width push-ups (NWPP) elicited triceps brachii EMG activity of 5.11 ± 1.97 mV and 105.83 ± 18.54 %MVC.
In a study of a 25-year-old male gymnast, shoulder-width push-ups (SWPP) produced triceps brachii EMG activity of 3.91 ± 1.36 mV and 74.32 ± 16.9 %MVC.

source: data\push-up\Comparison of Muscle Activation and Kinematic Analysis in Narrow-base and Shoulder-width Push-up Variations in Gymnast.pdf [part 1/8]

core_principles.text: Narrow-base push-ups elicit greater triceps brachii activation compared to shoulder-width push-ups, making them highly effective for targeting the triceps.
Shoulder-width push-ups show higher activation in the pectoralis major and anterior deltoid, making them suitable for general chest and shoulder strength development.
Narrow-based push-ups enhance shoulder stability and triceps strength, which benefits movements requiring narrow arm positions.

specific_findings.text: A study by Mankowski et al. (2016) compared narrow-based and shoulder-width push-ups over a 12-week training period in collegiate gymnasts, finding narrow-based push-ups elicited greater triceps brachii activation and shoulder-width showed higher activation in the pectoralis major.

A 2019 study by Jang et al. found that narrow-based push-ups led to significantly higher activation of the triceps brachii, while shoulder-width push-ups showed increased activation of the pectoralis major and anterior deltoid among elite gymnasts.

Simpson and Drury (2018) found that narrow-based push-ups enhanced shoulder stability and triceps strength, which directly benefited gymnasts during movements requiring narrow arm positions like the planche and handstand push-up.

core_principles.text: Narrow-based push-ups are highly effective for isolating the triceps and building endurance in the anterior deltoid and rotator cuff.
Shoulder-width push-ups provide a broader base of support, which improves postural control and reduces the risk of improper alignment during high-repetition sets.
Shoulder-width push-ups are superior for targeting and building endurance in the pectoralis major and overall chest musculature.
Incorporating both narrow-based and shoulder-width push-ups into a training regimen helps develop balanced upper-body endurance and joint stability.

common_mistakes.text: Losing postural control and experiencing improper alignment during high-repetition sets, especially when fatigued.

specific_findings.text: Jang et al. (2019) concluded that narrow-based push-ups are superior for triceps isolation, while shoulder-width push-ups provide a more balanced upper-body workout.

An EMG study by Chen and Yu (2021) indicated that narrow-based push-ups were superior for triceps recruitment even under fatigued conditions, while shoulder-width push-ups offered better postural control due to a broader base of support.

A 10-week endurance training study by Muller et al. (2020) on adolescent gymnasts found that narrow-based push-up training increased fatigue resistance in the triceps and anterior deltoid, whereas shoulder-width push-up training improved endurance in the pectoralis major.

Tanaka and Yamada (2022) found that narrow-based push-ups increased endurance in the stabilizing muscles of the shoulder, particularly the rotator cuff, while shoulder-width push-ups enhanced chest endurance.

consequences.text: Failing to maintain proper muscle balance and alignment increases the risk of overuse injuries in high-stress areas like the rotator cuff, shoulder girdle, and elbow joints.

core_principles.text: Incorporate both narrow-based and shoulder-width push-ups to ensure balanced development of the upper body and reduce the risk of overuse injuries.
Perform narrow-based push-ups to place greater emphasis on the triceps and shoulder stabilizers, which are crucial for preventing injuries during pressing movements.
Perform shoulder-width push-ups to engage a broader range of muscles, including the pectoralis major and anterior deltoid.
Utilize narrow-based push-ups during rehabilitation for rotator cuff injuries to rebuild strength without overloading the shoulder joint prematurely.

specific_findings.text: A study by Lee et al. (2017) found that narrow-based push-ups improved shoulder stability by strengthening the triceps and rotator cuff muscles to maintain proper joint alignment during overhead movements.

Rodriguez and Mendes (2023) found that narrow-based push-ups were particularly effective in the rehabilitation phase for athletes with rotator cuff injuries, allowing them to rebuild strength without premature shoulder joint overload.

Kim et al. (2019) found that narrow-based push-ups significantly improved gymnasts' ability to perform planche progressions, as triceps activation directly transferred to the required elbow extension.
Kim et al. (2019) found that shoulder-width push-ups benefited gymnasts performing dynamic skills, such as vaults and ring swings, where chest and shoulder strength were more important.

consequences.text: Uncorrected muscle imbalances from lacking push-up variation can lead to conditions such as rotator cuff strains, elbow tendinitis, and shoulder impingements.

core_principles.text: For a shoulder-width push-up, position the hands shoulder-width apart, directly under the shoulder joint.
For a narrow-width push-up, position the hands directly beneath the sternum.
Maintain an aligned body in a prone position with the feet on the ground.
Perform push-ups in controlled cycles, such as a fixed 2-second repetition rate starting from the top position.

specific_findings.text: A study of a single 25-year-old male gymnastic player (65 kg) compared the EMG response of the pectoralis major and triceps brachii during narrow-width and shoulder-width push-ups.
The push-up cycle was standardized using a metronome to fix the repetition rate at 2 seconds, starting from the top position.

core_principles.text: Hand placement during push-ups significantly impacts muscle activation, particularly in the triceps brachii.
Narrow-width push-ups generate higher electromyography (EMG) activity in the triceps brachii compared to shoulder-width push-ups.
A standard push-up involves flexing the elbows until the chest approaches the floor, followed by extending the elbows back to the initial position.

common_mistakes.text: Using a narrow-width hand position can restrict the elbow joint's range of motion during the push-up.

specific_findings.text: The average elbow joint angle was found to be 139.81 degrees in the shoulder-width push-up (SWPP) and 135.22 degrees in the narrow-width push-up (NWPP).
The range of motion in the wide-width push-up (WWPP) spans from 164.99 to 96.91 degrees, whereas the narrow-width push-up (NWPP) spans from 154.45 to 118.23 degrees.
The coefficient of correlation between elbow joint angle alteration and triceps EMG amplitude is 0.099 during NWPP and 0.882 during SWPP.
The mean triceps brachii EMG RMS value was 19.97 +/- 0.39 for SWPP and 21.04 +/- 0.26 for NWPP.

Right hand triceps EMG response was higher than the left hand during both push-up variations (SWPP-Right: 21.19 +/- 0.84, NWPP-Right: 22.75 +/- 0.23, SWPP-Left: 18.66 +/- 0.53, NWPP-Left: 19.33 +/- 0.71).

consequences.text: Restricting the range of motion during narrow-width push-ups develops and concentrates the load on the elbow joint.

core_principles.text: Narrow-width push-ups target the triceps more effectively by increasing triceps muscle activation and requiring a deeper range of elbow movement.
Shoulder-width push-ups distribute the load more evenly between the shoulders and elbows, making them highly suitable for general upper-body conditioning.
Achieving deeper elbow flexion during push-ups increases the mechanical load and muscular demand on the triceps.

specific_findings.text: During narrow-width push-ups, the elbow extension angle was 154.45 ± 3.96 degrees and the flexion angle was 118.23 ± 11.51 degrees.
During shoulder-width push-ups, the elbow extension angle was 164.99 ± 3.09 degrees and the flexion angle was 96.91 ± 6.20 degrees.
Narrow-width push-ups recruit more motor units and result in higher %MVC in the triceps compared to shoulder-width push-ups.

consequences.text: Performing narrow-width push-ups places greater localized strain on the elbow joint.
Failing to reach deep elbow flexion reduces the mechanical load and contractile demand placed on the triceps muscle.

core_principles.text: Narrow width push-ups are more effective for targeting the triceps brachii due to the greater internal moment required at the elbow joint.
Standard width push-ups provide a more balanced upper-body workout and elicit more pectoralis major activity, making them better for overall chest development.

specific_findings.text: Research by Simpson and Drury (2018) indicated that standard width push-ups may elicit more pectoralis major activity, supporting the variation for overall chest development.
